column5: Imagine… you wake up, and the sky is counting down.
Above every city, every ocean, every desert.
And nobody knows… what happens when they reach zero.
It starts on an ordinary morning.
In Tokyo, it's nine at night.
The numbers burn between the stars.
Within minutes, every phone on Earth is pointing up.
Any single object in the sky can only be seen from about half of the planet at a time.
The full Moon is only about half a degree wide.
Your fingernail, at arm's length, can cover it.
At the Moon's distance, a readable countdown would be thousands of kilometres wide.
Whatever this is… it is not a sign hanging in space.
Every telescope on Earth is pointed at it.
Stock markets crash in the first hour.
We have feared a date before.
Before the year two thousand, the world spent an estimated three hundred billion dollars on the Y2K bug.
That was one date on a calendar.
This one is written across the sky.
Places of worship fill up, all over the world, all at once.
Our brains stop reacting to a threat that never seems to arrive.
We even built a clock like this ourselves.
In nineteen forty-seven: the Doomsday Clock.
It started at seven minutes to midnight.
In twenty twenty-six, it was set to eighty-five seconds.
The closest it has ever been.
Most people… never even looked at it.
Now nobody is used to it anymore.
Some fly home to their parents.
Others throw the biggest parties in history.
Strangers start talking on the street.
A palliative nurse once wrote down the biggest regret of dying patients.
Not living the life they really wanted.
Eight billion people… quiet, at exactly the same moment.
The numbers fade… and the sky is just the sky again.
For one year, everyone knew their time was limited.
An eighty-year life is only about four thousand weeks.
So… if your numbers were in the sky… what would you do with the time left?
